changeEvents.title: Context Collection
changeEvents.description: The craft of agentic biography is collecting context, and the test is whether the agent actually reads its corpus before it speaks.

changeEvents.title: Forms Are Projections
changeEvents.description: A printed biography, a video tribute, a chapter: forms are rendered from the corpus and never stored inside it.

changeEvents.title: Moments and the Timeline
changeEvents.description: A moment is a bounded thing that happened. The timeline is a generated index over moments. Neither is a transcript.

changeEvents.title: The Biographical Ontology
changeEvents.description: Six shapes hold a captured life: profile, transcripts, characters, moments, the timeline, and letters. Everything else is a projection.

changeEvents.title: Transcripts
changeEvents.description: The append-only ground truth of a biography: the person's words verbatim, stamped to the minute, filed with the question that elicited them.

changeEvents.title: Don't Overengineer the Ontology
changeEvents.description: The ontology earns new shapes on the second instance, never the first. Six shapes cover a life; a taxonomy kills a collection.

changeEvents.title: The Question Is Part of the Record
changeEvents.description: Every transcript files the question that elicited it. An answer without its question is half a record.
